study.title: Psalm 15 Who can dwell in the presence of the Lord?
study.overview: This psalm presents a solemn question and then describes the character of who can stand before God. The text does not deal first with external rites, but of concrete integrity: walking sincerely, practicing justice, speaking truth in the heart, controlling speech, not harming others, honoring those who fear the Lord, keeping the word even when it costs, and refusing unjust gains. The closure of the salty connects this way of life to stability: those who live this way will not be shaken.

outline.title: The question about who can remain with God
outline.explanation: The first verse opens with a question that directs the reader to the privilege and seriousness of dwelling in the tent of the Lord and on the mountain of his holiness. The emphasis is on who is worthy of this communion, not in mere social position or religious inheritance.

outline.title: Portrait of the Right Character
outline.explanation: In verses 2 to 4, the psalm answers by the description of a whole life: to walk sincerely, to do what is right, to speak the truth, not to use the tongue to hurt, not to defame the neighbor, to despise what is morally reprobable and to honor those who fear the Lord. It also includes fidelity to the given word, even when the fulfillment brings personal injury.

outline.title: Justice in relations and the promise of firmness
outline.explanation: The last verse completes the portrait with economic and judicial practices: not exploiting the needy through abusive interest or corrupt justice with bribery against the innocent. The promised result is stability: whoever lives like this will not be shaken.

study.context: The notes place this psalm between texts that emphasize integrity and purity, and present it as a poem of wisdom that contrasts the path of the godly with the conduct of the ungodly. It is also possible to read it, in the notes, as a description of those who can live in the presence of God, using the image of the tent and the holy mountain to speak of communion with the Lord. Some interpretive readings bring this language closer to the community of faith and hope of permanence before God, but this should be understood as an interpretation, not as a unique explicit statement of the text.
study.theology: Theologically, psalm teaches that closeness to God is not treated as an automatic right, but as a privilege linked to a life consistent with divine holiness. The biblical faith here is visible in concrete relations: truth in words, righteousness in actions, mastery of language, honor to godly, fidelity in compromises and justice without exploitation. The psalm also unites ethics and spiritual security: the whole life does not buy salvation, but is described as the way of those who stand firm before the Lord. In Protestant evangelical reading, this shows that practical holiness is the expected fruit of those who seek God, and not just religious appearance.

scholarViews.insight: The psalm is a poem of wisdom that contrasts the lifestyle of the godly with the actions of the wicked, and the question about who inhabits the presence of God introduces a description of the qualities of the godly character.
The question of the psalm serves to investigate who can be a citizen of Zion and is followed by an answer that describes the path of holiness and honesty as the way of entering life.

The psalm answers the question of who is an appropriate member of the people of God; in verses 2 to 5, the focus lies on the practical conduct of the just, especially its integrity in relations and its refusal to exploit.

questions: What aspects of your speech and your relationships show today that you want to dwell in the presence of the Lord?
Is there any area in which you need to correct unfair practices, unfulfilled promises, or exploration attitudes?
How does this psalm change the way you understand spiritual stability: as an external appearance or as the fruit of an entire life before God?
study.practice: Examine this week his life on three fronts: words, money and relationships. Decide to tell the truth more clearly, to fulfill what he promised even at personal cost and avoid any advantage that harms others. If you occupy a position of influence, use it to honor those who fear the Lord and protect the innocent, and not to press, manipulate or profit unfairly. Pray that the Lord may make his life consistent with his presence.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided are brief and do not allow you to safely reconstruct the entire historical background of the psalm. There are also interpretative differences between the commentators regarding the scope of the images of tent, holy hill and final stability; therefore, these readings were presented as interpretations, not as absolute conclusions. It is not possible to confirm, only with the material given, additional details about authorship, date or liturgical context of the psalm.
